i.norm:
Verifies the legacy {@code stopAtNonOption} flag behaviour of {@link DefaultParser}.

When {@code stopAtNonOption = true} the parser halts at the first unrecognised token and appends it together with all remaining tokens to the argument list rather than throwing. When {@code stopAtNonOption = false} an {@link UnrecognizedOptionException} is thrown instead.
--- Arrange --- Define three recognised single-letter options with long-form aliases.
Input contains three recognised options followed by one rogue option (-d) and two plain arguments. -d is intentionally unknown to exercise the stopAtNonOption boundary.
--- Act (stopAtNonOption = true) --- Parsing must not throw: the parser should stop at -d and collect it together with the remaining tokens as plain arguments.
--- Assert (stopAtNonOption = true) --- Exactly -a, -b, -c were recognised as options.
The rogue token (-d) and the two plain arguments are captured as args.
--- Act & Assert (stopAtNonOption = false) --- When stop-at-non-option is disabled, the unrecognised -d must cause an UnrecognizedOptionException whose message identifies the offending flag.
